#### Main Title
**Our Approach**

#### Left Column Text

**Once appointed, we will support SuperX AIHUB from the outset of the project lifecycle, providing project management and advisory services from early project setup through completion. Our approach is focused on establishing clear governance, disciplined project controls, and effective coordination to support safe, predictable, and well-managed project delivery.**

At project commencement, we will organize a comprehensive stakeholder meeting involving the Client, the consultant team, and other key project participants. The purpose of this meeting is to establish communication protocols, confirm roles and responsibilities, and ensure alignment on project objectives and delivery expectations. This early alignment supports efficient decision-making and provides a consistent framework for project execution. Project governance, reporting requirements, and workflows will be formalized through the Project Execution Plan.

We will support the Client and consultant team by providing guidance on coordination with local authorities, utility providers, and statutory agencies. This includes advising on typical processes, sequencing considerations, and key milestones related to power supply, water supply and discharge, and construction and building permits. Authority and utility interfaces will be monitored in relation to the overall project program to support alignment with construction and commissioning activities.

#### Right Column Text

During the design phase, we will work closely with the consultant team to support a structured and coordinated design process. Design development will be reviewed with consideration for constructability, compliance with project requirements, and readiness for procurement, construction, and commissioning. Particular focus will be placed on identifying critical systems and interfaces early and managing design decisions in a manner that supports schedule, cost, quality, and operational readiness objectives.

Throughout procurement and contractor onboarding, we will assist the Client in managing tender processes and contractor appointments in coordination with the Quantity Surveyor. This includes supporting the review of technical and commercial submissions, schedules, and key assumptions, and facilitating contractor onboarding to align execution planning with the overall project delivery strategy.

The PMC team will deliver the services outlined in this proposal throughout the construction lifecycle and will maintain a regular on-site presence. The team will attend key site meetings and site walks with the contractor and the Client’s team to monitor progress, safety, and quality. Daily and weekly observations will be captured and communicated, supported by consolidated monthly reporting covering project status, key risks, and required actions. The team will also assist the Client with progress claim verification and review of variation and change requests.

Throughout delivery, we will coordinate closely with the consultant team and contractor to support timely resolution of interface issues and maintain progress in accordance with the approved program. Regular site inspections will be performed, key inspections and tests will be witnessed, and installation works will be reviewed for compliance with approved drawings, specifications, and submittals. Critical equipment delivery and installation will be monitored, test results reviewed, and quality and commissioning records maintained to support commissioning and integrated systems testing readiness.

At the final stage of the project, we will oversee the testing and commissioning process in collaboration with the consultants and commissioning agent to confirm that systems are validated and operational. Upon project completion, we will facilitate the closeout and handover process, including final inspections and defect resolution, and support the delivery of required documentation such as as-built drawings, operation and maintenance manuals, warranties, and commissioning records.

Key elements of our approach include:
* Early establishment of project governance and communication protocols
* Structured coordination and advisory support for authority and utility interfaces
* Consistent monitoring of safety, quality, schedule, and cost performance
* Commissioning-focused delivery to support Ready-for-Service and orderly handover

##### **Design and Construction Sequencing Understanding**
> The SuperX AIhub program is being delivered under a Design-Build (DB) model to achieve schedule certainty and single-point accountability. While this model enables fast-track delivery, it introduces material risks if design, procurement, and construction are not governed as an integrated sequence. In a DB environment, loss of Owner control can occur quickly if design intent, performance requirements, and change discipline are not clearly enforced.
> 
> A primary delivery challenge is therefore maintaining strong Owner-side governance without interfering in the DB Contractor’s design responsibility. This requires clear stage-gated design reviews, early design maturity for mission-critical systems, defined design freeze points for long-lead items, and disciplined change control. Informal direction or late decision-making would undermine both schedule and commercial outcomes.
> 
> RFS achievement further depends on the coordinated delivery of all enabling infrastructure, not just the data halls. Power substations, water systems, security infrastructure, and external works must be sequenced in parallel and aligned to commissioning readiness. If not actively governed, these supporting assets can become late critical-path drivers. Effective sequencing therefore demands early works enablement, parallel execution strategies, and progressive, zone-based commissioning aligned to RFS milestones.

##### **Initial Risks and Mitigations**
> Under a Design-Build model, a key risk is scope ambiguity between Employer’s Requirements and Contractor execution. In high-density, liquid-cooled data centers, this risk is magnified by the need for early technical certainty across power, cooling, controls, and monitoring systems. Late design changes or incomplete definition can result in claims, rework, and commissioning delays. Mitigation requires early validation of design assumptions, strict design freeze discipline for critical systems, and formalized change governance that protects Owner outcomes while maintaining Contractor accountability.
> 
> Thailand-specific authority and utility dependencies present additional delivery risk. The project relies on timely coordination with multiple agencies for power, water, discharge approvals, inspections, and statutory certifications. Delays in authority processes can directly impact commissioning and RFS. These risks are mitigated through early engagement, parallel submissions where permitted, inspection readiness planning, and treating authority milestones as fixed schedule constraints.
> 
> Site and environmental risks in Rayong including variable ground conditions, seasonal rainfall, and flooding potential, also require early mitigation. Without proactive planning, these factors can disrupt early works and external infrastructure, with downstream impact to MEP installation and commissioning. Early investigations, flood mitigation planning, and seasonally informed sequencing are therefore critical to schedule protection.
> 
> Finally, commissioning and Integrated Systems Testing (IST) represent a material RFS risk if underestimated or compressed late in the program. For a high-density, liquid-cooled facility, commissioning must be progressive, structured, and governed as a core delivery phase. Early strategy definition, zone-based testing, clear acceptance criteria, and disciplined issue closure are essential to achieving RFS without late-stage disruption.

---

##### **Turner’s Value and Differentiation**
> Turner’s proposed Project Management approach is specifically structured to address these challenges. We bring disciplined DB governance, RFS-driven sequencing, and proactive risk management that protects SuperX AIhub’s schedule, cost, and operational objectives. Our role is to maintain Owner control without diluting DB accountability, integrate design, construction, commissioning, and authority requirements into a single delivery framework, and ensure that every decision is evaluated against its impact on Ready-For-Service. This is how Turner delivers certainty in complex, high-risk data center programs.

### Main Body Text Transcription

"Turner is committed to the tenets of 5S thinking and this is a critical component of Turner’s embrace of the Lean culture of working. The lean approach to construction can be broken down into five steps - the Five S’s - that become an everyday part of how the team approaches the project.

**The Five S’s are:**

**SORT** – Go through a designated work area and sort out the necessary from the unnecessary. Necessary is defined by frequency of use. If it is not used daily or weekly, it probably doesn’t need to be kept anywhere near the operations. Items that are necessary are kept and all while the rest are disposed of, recycled or returned. Sorting is fun; it feels good to get rid of stuff!

**STRAIGHTEN** - Put everything (that was determined as necessary in Sorting) in a designated place and visually mark it. This is the critical step to eliminating time wasted in doing “treasure hunts.” Not only is a place established for every necessary item, but the actual location is based on how often it is used. The items we use most often are located closest to where we use them. Those used less often are farther away.

**SHINE** - Physically clean up the work area and deliberately pick up all parts and material that are out of place and return each to its assigned place.=
